key_insight: KANEx uses the interpretable structure of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) to ground both visual saliency and language explanations, aiming to make medical AI explanations more trustworthy.
clinical_relevance: For chest X-ray workflows, this approach could improve how clinicians understand why a model predicts a finding by linking text explanations to more faithful image regions.
method: Builds KANEx, a framework that connects KAN interpretability to downstream vision-language explanation generation.
Introduces KAN-Map, a heatmap method derived directly from KAN models instead of gradient-based approximations.
Feeds KAN-derived grounded context into VLMs to improve explanation quality.
evidence_signal: On the MIMIC-CXR dataset, KAN-based models with ResNet/ViT baselines showed improved semantic similarity, more faithful saliency maps, and about 10% better visual localization and reasoning quality.
watch_item: The approach depends on effective integration of KANs with VLMs and should still be validated across broader datasets, clinical settings, and real-world deployment conditions.
paper_title: KANEx: Translating Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks' Interpretability to Medical Explainability
